sentences.text: Symmorium resembled Stethacanthus in size and general appearance, yet it lacked the distinctive spine-brush complex on its first dorsal fin.
Edward Drinker Cope first described this genus in 1893.
It belongs to the family Stethacanthidae.
This fish inhabited waters in the United States and Russia during the Devonian and Carboniferous periods.
Its fossils date from the Famennian to the Gzhelian stages, spanning between 372.15 and 298.9 million years ago.
Scientists debate whether Symmorium and Stethacanthus represent male and female forms of the same species or distinct genera.
Some researchers hypothesize that Symmorium was the female form of Stethacanthus.
